text: Your girlfriend or wife wants to take a break from their relationship. What do you do next? Let's break it down using this story. I gave my wife a break two weeks ago. What is next? The guy is 33 and the wife is 32. So right away, quick reality check for you guys. If you are in a relationship where you need to take a break from each other, that already tells you something is seriously wrong. Healthy relationships don't need breaks. They might need conversations or compromises, but not separation. A break is usually just a slow-motion breakup where people are afraid to say it out loud. Now, a quick side note before we go further. If you have questions, dating situations, or relationship stories you want my take on, you can direct message me here or on Telegram. My wife and I have been together for 10 years. The last couple of years, she's had a foot out of the door as things got rough between us for a bit, and she's never been able to let it go. She most definitely suffers from avoidant attachment, and I think I am anxious attachment. I found out she was flirting with another guy on Facebook Messenger, but I caught it quick, like the second day. And I know she was ashamed and said it was because she was hurt, even though all I do is try to have a good relationship with her. So he caught his wife flirting with another guy on Facebook, and almost says it proudly, I caught it quickly on the second date. Man, that's not something to be proud of. She was emotionally cheating on you. Catching it early doesn't make it any better. It just means it happened. A married woman talking to another man behind your back does not respect you, and you cannot build a healthy relationship with someone who doesn't respect you. If you tolerate that, you are teaching her there are no real consequences to her cheating on you and disrespecting you. But I decided at that point I was going to go stay with my brother, and I told her I would not come back until she was all in on us and wanting to do the work. I've been trying to give her all the space in the world to think and process. I know this has been hard on her. She's sad every time I see her to pick up my kids. Oh, damn, they're kids. I know she loves me, but she keeps saying that she just remembers the way I made her feel in the past. It's been two weeks now today that I've been gone. How long do I wait before I make my next move? Okay, guys, I will stop here. If you are curious, the rest of the story is on your screen. So, men, you don't wait. The next move is very clear. You end the relationship. You stop chasing clarity from someone who already, as you put it, has one foot out of the door, and you start rebuilding your life. That means divorce, clear boundaries, focusing on your kids, and keeping contact with your wife strictly about that. Then you work on yourself. Career, health, dates, hobbies, friends, meeting new people. Step by step, you slowly rebuild what little self-respect you have left, if there is any left. And only from that position can you actually create a life you don't feel the need to escape from.
